exercise.name: Tate Press
library_steps: Lie on a flat bench, dumbbells held straight up, inner ends almost touching.
Bend your elbows out to the sides to bring the dumbbells to your chest.
Press them back up by straightening your arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Flat bench, palms toward the feet, dumbbells held straight up end to end; elbows bend OUT to the sides (~115 deg) so the inner ends of the dumbbells tip down onto the middle of the chest; press back up. Triceps does the work.

setup.target: Flat on the bench, feet flat on the floor.
Palms face the feet (pronated), dumbbells pressed straight up over the chest, inner ends almost touching, elbows pointing out.
setup.why: Defines the Tate press; elbows out is what makes it different from a skull crusher.

movement.end: 115 deg (inner dumbbell ends on the chest)

movement.measure: upper arm from the torso side line
0 = out to the side, +90 = straight up from the chest
movement.start: 93 deg (hands slightly inward so the ends nearly touch)
movement.end: 45 deg (elbows drift out to the sides)

muscles.muscle: Triceps brachii (medial and lateral heads stressed)
muscles.emg: No Tate press EMG found. Elbow-extension exercises reach 62-87% of the triangle push-up (S2). Coaching source says it targets the medial head (S1).

muscles.muscle: Pectoralis major / anterior deltoid (hold the arms up)

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows point toward the feet; dumbbells come down like a close-grip press.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Loses the elbows-out pattern that defines the exercise.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms swing down to the bench instead of the elbows bending.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Becomes a press; triceps work drops.

sources.citation: Muscle & Strength. Dumbbell Tate Press exercise profile.
sources.what_it_gave: Lie supine, dumbbells pressed up, palms facing forward (toward the feet), elbows out to the sides; bend the elbows to lower the dumbbells to the chest, extend to return. Targets the medial triceps head, 10-15 reps.

sources.citation: Boehler B, Porcari JP, Kline D, Hendrix CR, Foster C, Anders M. 2011. ACE-sponsored research: best triceps exercises. ACE Certified News, Aug 2011.
sources.what_it_gave: Triceps EMG across eight exercises (62-100% of triangle push-up); no Tate press tested.

clip_check.check: Start: arms vertical, dumbbells end to end, gap 0-5 cm, not overlapping
End: elbows out to the sides, inner ends touch the chest, dumbbells not inside chest or each other
Palms toward the feet in both pictures
Back on pad, feet on floor
Triceps strongest red in both pictures
